City Council Approves Downtown Pedestrian Pilot After Months of Debate

RIVERTON — The Riverton City Council voted 5–2 on Tuesday to launch a six-month pilot that will restrict private vehicle traffic on three blocks of Main Street, a move supporters say will boost foot traffic for local businesses and improve public safety.

Under the plan, the affected stretch of Main Street will be closed to through-traffic from 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily, starting April 15. Deliveries will be permitted during designated morning hours, and residents who live within the pilot zone will be issued limited access passes.

Councilmember Elena Park, who introduced the proposal, called the vote “a practical test with clear benchmarks.” City staff will track pedestrian counts, nearby sales-tax receipts, collision reports and emergency response times, and will present an interim update at the three-month mark.

Some business owners applauded the decision. “Weekends already feel like a street fair,” said Marco Ruiz, who runs a café near the proposed closure. “If the city manages loading zones and signage well, I think it can bring more customers.”

Others remain skeptical. “I’m worried about customers who rely on quick stops,” said Dana Whitfield, owner of a hardware store on Main. “If parking becomes confusing, people will go elsewhere.”

The Riverton Fire Department said it can maintain response times with minor route adjustments, though Chief Carla Nguyen urged the city to enforce keeping the corridor clear for emergency vehicles.

The pilot will automatically expire in mid-October unless the council votes to extend or make the changes permanent.
